summary: Johan Nicolai Madvig worked in linguistics. He studied at Frederiksborg Gymnasium og HF (~1817–1820) and the University of Copenhagen (~1820–1826), where he later held a post from circa 1829 to 1879.

Johan van Manen worked in Tibetology and Indology. He served at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (1909–1916), the National Library of India (1918–1921), the Indian Museum, Kolkata (1922), and The Asiatic Society (1923–1939).

Johann Albrecht Bernhard von Dorn worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. After studying at Halle-Wittenberg and Leipzig, he held posts at the University of Kharkiv (1829–1835), Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences (1835), and Asiatic Museum (1842).

Johann Andreas Schmeller studied at the University of Munich (~1801–1803). He later held posts at the Real Instituto Militar Pestalozziano, Bavarian Cadet Corps, Bavarian State Library, and the University of Munich (1828, 1846).

Johann August Vullers worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Giessen, Bonn, and Halle-Wittenberg under Windischmann, Freytag, von Schlegel, Silvestre de Sacy, Quatremère, Abel-Rémusat, and Bopp, later serving at Bonn and Giessen.
Johann Caspar von Orelli worked in linguistics. He held posts at Bündner Kantonsschule (~1819–1831), Carolinum Zürich (~1831–1833), and the University of Zurich (~1833–1849).

Johann Christian Christoph Rüdiger worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1768) and later served there as a Privatdozent (1777) and associate professor (1791).

Johann Christoph Adelung worked in linguistics. He studied at Kloster Berge school and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and later served at Evangelisches Ratsgymnasium Erfurt (1758) and the Saxon State and University Library Dresden (1787).

Johann Detloff Prochnow worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Greifswald (1837–1840) and held posts with the Church Mission Society (1843) and Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church (~1858–1869).

Johann Dietrich Ludwig de Vries worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Utrecht, Amsterdam, Lille, and Bonn under Willem Caland, Jos. Schrijnen, Hermann Jacobi, and Willibald Kirfel, and served as deputy professor at Stellenbosch University (1923).

Johann Friedrich Blumenbach worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Ernestinum Gotha, the University of Jena, and the University of Göttingen, where he later held a post from circa 1775 to 1840.
Johann Friedrich Herbart was a philosopher. He studied at the University of Jena (~1794–1797) and held a post at the University of Göttingen (~1802–1809).
Johann Friedrich Kleuker worked in religious studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (1770) and was Professor of Theology at Kiel University (1798).

Johann Gildemeister was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Göttingen and Bonn under Krummacher, Ewald, Freytag, Lassen, and Schlegel. He held posts at the University of Bonn (1839, 1844–1889) and the University of Marburg (1845, 1848–1858).

Johann Gottfried Eichhorn worked in religious studies, history/archaeology, and linguistics. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at Göttingen (1770–1774) and held professorships at the University of Jena (1775) and the University of Göttingen (1788).

Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Greifswald and under Silvestre de Sacy and Chézy in Paris. He held academic posts at Greifswald (1814–1817, 1824–1850) and Jena (1817–1824).

Johann Gottfried von Herder worked in philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied under Immanuel Kant at Königsberg. His posts included Riga Cathedral School, the University of Latvia, Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach, and Wilhelm-Ernst-Gymnasium Weimar.
Johann Gottlieb Rhode worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Helmstedt (~1781–1785) and the University of Jena (~1821), and taught at Kriegsschule Berlin from 1809.

Johann Gustav Stickel worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Jena and under Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten, Andreas Gottlieb Hoffmann, and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, later serving as professor at Jena (1830–1836).

Johann Heinrich Kalthoff worked in Indology. He studied at Münster, Bonn, and under Silvestre de Sacy and Abel-Rémusat. He held posts at Gymnasium Paulinum (1831) and the University of Münster (1830–1839).
